subtitle: On the storm-worn frontier of Bengal, a general builds power with verses, not walls.

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of Paragal Khan on a Chittagong hill, Kavindra seated below with palm-leaf manuscript
panels.action: Paragal Khan stands armored on a wind-beaten rise above the Chittagong coast, looking toward distant forests and sea, while Kavindra Parameshwar sits cross-legged beside him, ready with a palm-leaf manuscript, village and fort stretching behind them.

dialogue.text: On Bengal’s far eastern edge, General Paragal Khan backs a Bengali Mahabharata—proof that in the sultanate, culture itself could be frontier strategy.

i18n.hi: बंगाल के सुदूर पूरबी किनारे पर, जनरल परगल ख़ाँ बांग्ला महाभरत का साथ देता है—सुबहानत में सरहद की नीति भी संस्कृति बन सकती है।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye over riverine Bengal, drifting east toward Chittagong
panels.action: Broad rivers wind through misty plains dotted with villages and temple spires, then give way eastward to darker hills, thick forests and the coastal belt of Chittagong under a hazy dawn.

dialogue.text: In the early 1500s, Bengal’s sultans ruled from Gaur and Pandua. But the sharpest edge of their world lay far away, in the forests and harbors of Chittagong.

i18n.hi: १५०० के शुरुआती सालों में, बंगाल के सुल्तान गौड़ और पांडुआ से हुकूमत करते हैं। पर उनकी दुनिया की सबसे नुकीली धार दूर है—चटगाँव के जंगलों और बंदरगाहों में।

panels.shot: mid-shot inside a frontier fort hall, Paragal Khan in command council
panels.action: Inside a timber-roofed hall of a frontier fort near Fatehabad, Paragal Khan sits at the head of a low table, armored but unhelmeted, conferring with local officers and landholding chiefs whose dress mixes Persian and Bengali styles.

dialogue.text: After campaigns against Arakan and along the Chittagong littoral, Paragal Khan emerges as the sultanate’s trusted frontier commander, governing these contested lands in the name of the Gaur court.

i18n.hi: अराकान पर और चटगाँव के समुंदर-तट पर लड़ाइयों के बाद, परगल ख़ाँ सरहद का भरोसेमंद सेनापति बनकर उभरता है, गौड़ दरबार के नाम पर इन छिने हुए इलाकों पर राज चलाता है।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Paragal Khan listening to a Brahmin recite in a courtyard
panels.action: In the open courtyard of Paragalpur, Paragal Khan reclines on a raised platform, listening intently as Kavindra Parameshwar, in simple Brahmin robes, recites Sanskrit verses from a palm-leaf manuscript to a small circle of listeners.

dialogue.text: Around him, landed elites and Brahmin poets recite the Mahabharata in Sanskrit. The epic already lives in Bengal—but not yet in the everyday tongue of the villages he must hold.

i18n.hi: चारों ओर ज़मींदार और ब्राह्मण कवि संस्कृत में महाभरत सुनाते हैं। महाकाव्य बंगाल में तो ज़िंदा है—पर उन गाँवों की रोज़ की ज़ुबान में नहीं, जिन्हें उसे थामना है।

panels.shot: tight two-shot of Paragal Khan and Kavindra in quiet conversation under a tree
panels.action: Under a banyan tree near the fort, Paragal Khan leans forward in measured curiosity while Kavindra Parameshwar gestures respectfully with a manuscript, the low hum of the nearby bazaar fading into the background.

dialogue.speaker: Paragal Khan
dialogue.text: Our soldiers and farmers know these stories. But they do not hear them in their own words.

i18n.hi: हमारे सिपाही और किसान इन कहानियों को जानते हैं। पर ये उनकी अपनी बोली में नहीं गूँजतीं।

panels.shot: mid-shot of Kavindra in his study with palm leaves, lamp light
panels.action: In a modest scholar’s room lit by an oil lamp, Kavindra Parameshwar sits surrounded by stacked palm leaves and ink pots, eyes focused as he selects passages from a Sanskrit Mahabharata manuscript laid open before him.

dialogue.text: Manuscript colophons remember Kavindra as the poet, Parameshwar as the hand that shapes verses. His task is not a full translation, but a selective Bengali Mahabharata for this frontier world.

i18n.hi: पांडुलिपियों के अंत में कविन्द्र को कवि और परमेś्वर को कलम चलाने वाला याद किया गया है। उसका काम पूरी तर्जुमा नहीं, इस सरहद की दुनिया के लिए चुनी हुई बांग्ला महाभरत है।

panels.shot: low-angle of Paragal Khan issuing an order to attendants bearing palm leaves and coin
panels.action: Inside the audience hall, Paragal Khan sits upright in a carved chair, right hand raised decisively as attendants step forward carrying palm leaves, cloth-wrapped coins and ink, symbolizing dedicated patronage to Kavindra’s work.

dialogue.text: Paragal Khan does not take up the pen himself. The records call him patron—he orders resources, time, security, and payment so Kavindra can compose in Middle Bengali under his protection.

i18n.hi: परगल ख़ाँ खुद कलम नहीं उठाता। रिकार्ड उसे सरपरस्त कहते हैं—वह रसद, वक़्त, हिफ़ाज़त और मेहनताना तय करता है, ताकि कविन्द्र उसकी पनाह में मध्य बांग्ला में लिख सके।

panels.shot: close-up of a scribe’s hands copying Bengali verses from Kavindra’s dictation
panels.action: A scribe sits cross-legged beside Kavindra, carefully inscribing Bengali lines in rounded script onto fresh palm leaves, while Kavindra dictates, a faint view of Paragalpur’s village huts through the open doorway.

dialogue.text: Line by line, a Paragali Mahabharata takes shape. It carries the old Sanskrit story, but in the new sound of Middle Bengali that villagers, soldiers and minor chiefs can follow without a learned guide.

i18n.hi: पंक्ति-पंक्ति परागली महाभरत रूप लेती है। पुरानी संस्कृत कथा रहती है, पर आवाज़ नई है—मध्य बांग्ला, जिसे गाँव वाले, सिपाही और छोटे मुंशी भी बिना पंडित के समझ लें।

panels.shot: wide village evening scene, poet reciting, Paragal Khan watching from balcony
panels.action: At dusk in a village near Fatehabad, Kavindra stands on a low platform reciting Bengali Mahabharata verses to gathered farmers, women and children, while Paragal Khan observes quietly from a balcony of the fort above.

dialogue.text: Scholars later note: this is not a capital court performance, but a provincial one. In Paragalpur and Fatehabad, a Muslim military household backs Hindu epic recitation as part of its local public life.

i18n.hi: विद्वान बाद में नोट करते हैं: यह राजधानी दरबार की नहीं, सूबे की पेशकश है। परगलपुर और फ़तेहाबाद में एक मुस्लिम फ़ौजी घराना, अपनी लोक-ज़िंदगी का हिस्सा बनाकर, हिंदू महाकाव्य-पाठ को सहारा देता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Paragal Khan receiving local chiefs and Brahmins together
panels.action: In the fort’s reception hall, Paragal Khan greets a group of local Hindu chiefs and Brahmins; Kavindra stands among them with a manuscript, the mixed assembly clearly bound to the general’s seat of authority.

dialogue.text: By supporting Kavindra’s Bengali Mahabharata, Paragal Khan ties his frontier rule to the land’s existing networks: Brahmin literati, local magnates, and the shared epic that underpins their moral world.

i18n.hi: कविन्द्र की बांग्ला महाभरत का साथ देकर, परगल ख़ाँ अपनी सरहदी सत्ता को यहाँ के बने-बनाए जाल से बाँधता है—ब्राह्मण विद्वान, देसी सरदार, और वह साझा महाकाव्य जो उनकी नैतिक दुनिया की नींव है।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a manuscript colophon page held between hands
panels.action: A pair of careful hands holds open a palm-leaf manuscript, the colophon section visible, with names and dedicatory lines etched in neat script, while the faint silhouettes of fort walls appear in the background.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, manuscript colophons still whisper the arrangement: Paragal Khan as patron, Kavindra Parameshwar as poet, Chittagong’s frontier as the stage on which this Bengali Mahabharata was made.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद भी, पांडुलिपियों के अंत में वही फुसफुसाहट बची है—सरपरस्त परगल ख़ाँ, कवि कविन्द्र परमेś्वर, और चटगाँव की सरहद, जिस पर यह बांग्ला महाभरत गढ़ी गई।

panels.shot: wide shot of Paragalpur and Fatehabad landscape with fort, shrine, and river
panels.action: A panoramic view shows the fort at Paragalpur, nearby village shrines, a mosque dome, and the winding river near Fatehabad, all under a cloudy sky that hints at both monsoon storms and enduring calm.

dialogue.text: The work travels along rivers and roads. Copyists in other settlements make their own palm-leaf versions, so this selective Bengali Mahabharata threads through the eastern districts, beyond direct reach of Gaur.

i18n.hi: रचनाएँ नदियों और राहों पर चलती हैं। दूसरे कस्बों के नकलनवीस अपनी-अपनी ताड़-पत्तों की कापियाँ बनाते हैं, और यह चुनी हुई बांग्ला महाभरत पूरबी इलाक़ों में गुथती चली जाती है, गौड़ की सीधी पकड़ से बाहर।

panels.shot: medium shot of a younger man beside Paragal Khan, receiving a manuscript
panels.action: In a shaded chamber, an aging Paragal Khan hands a bound set of palm leaves to a younger noble, Chhuti Khan, who accepts them with reverence while Kavindra watches from the side, serene yet aware of the continuity.

dialogue.text: Sources mention Paragal Khan’s son, Chhuti Khan, continuing such patronage. The pattern outlives one general: frontier power is now linked to vernacular letters as well as to arms.

i18n.hi: मूलों में परगल ख़ाँ के बेटे, छुटी ख़ाँ का भी ज़िक्र है—वह भी ऐसी सरपरस्ती को आगे बढ़ाता है। ढाँचा एक जनरल से ज़्यादा देर जीता है: अब सरहद की ताक़त हथियारों के साथ-साथ लोक-लिपि से भी जुड़ी है।

panels.shot: close-up on an archivist’s table with multiple Kavindra Mahabharata leaves
panels.action: On a modern scholar’s worktable, several old palm-leaf manuscripts labeled as Kavindra or Paragali Mahabharata lie side by side, their scripts compared under soft light and careful hands.

dialogue.text: Recent manuscript studies stress its nature: not a complete rendering of all Mahabharata books, but a regional selection, shaped by local tastes and the needs of a frontier audience.

i18n.hi: नई पांडुलिपी रिसर्च बताती है: यह पूरी महाभरत नहीं, बल्कि एक इलाकाई चुनवाँ है, जो देसी पसंद और सरहदी श्रोताओं की ज़रूरतों से ढली है।

panels.shot: wide shot dissolving from fort to abstract map of sultanate cultural centers
panels.action: The image transitions from Paragalpur’s fort to an abstract map showing Gaur, Pandua, Chittagong and other centers linked by faint lines, suggesting networks of patronage and language across the Bengal Sultanate.

dialogue.text: Literary historians like Sukumar Sen and Sheldon Pollock see Paragal’s support as a key clue: Bengal’s vernacular Mahabharata tradition grows not only in royal courts, but in provincial military households as well.

i18n.hi: साहित्य-इतिहासकार सुकुमार सेन और शेल्डन पोलॉक जैसे लोग परगल के सहारे को अहम सुराग मानते हैं—बंगाल की लोक-भाषा महाभरत परंपरा सिर्फ़ शाही दरबार में नहीं, सूबाई फ़ौजी घरानों में भी पनपती है।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Kavindra reciting, his voice echoing over river at dusk
panels.action: Kavindra stands by a riverbank at dusk, reciting verses to a small group; the sound seems to carry over water and fields, while far in the background the silhouette of the fort anchors the scene.

dialogue.speaker: Kavindra Parameshwar
dialogue.text: Under many banners, dharma’s story still walks among the people.

i18n.hi: कितने ही झंडों के नीचे, धर्म की कहानी अब भी लोगों के बीच चलती फिरती है।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on Paragal Khan’s thoughtful profile overlooking his lands
panels.action: Paragal Khan stands on the ramparts of his frontier fort, gazing over forests, fields and distant hamlets, his face calm, hands resting on the stone as if weighing both the land and its stories.

dialogue.text: Today, Paragal Khan and Kavindra Parameshwar remind us that on a fragile frontier, culture can be policy: a shared language of epic and ethics that binds a borderland more quietly, but as firmly, as any wall.

i18n.hi: आज परगल ख़ाँ और कविन्द्र परमेś्वर याद दिलाते हैं कि नाज़ुक सरहद पर संस्कृति भी नीति हो सकती है—महाकाव्य और आचार की साझा ज़ुबान, जो चुपचाप पर उतनी ही मज़बूती से, सरहद को बाँध देती है जितनी कोई दीवार।

subtitle_i18n.en: On the storm-worn frontier of Bengal, a general builds power with verses, not walls.
subtitle_i18n.hi: तूफ़ानों से घिसी बंगाल की सरहद पर, एक जनरल दीवारों नहीं, शेरों से ताक़त बनाता है।
